title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for diabetes management.

HPI
The patient is a known case of type 2 diabetes mellitus presenting for a routine follow-up. The patient reports recent episodes of hyperglycemia. They have been managed with long-term insulin therapy and currently do not take any oral medications for their glucose levels. The patient notes that blood glucose readings have been inconsistent over the last month.

Medication List
- Insulin (long-term)

Exam
The patient appears in no acute distress. Physical examination reveals stable vital signs. Skin is intact with no new lesions. General appearance is consistent with a stable chronic condition.

Assessment
1. Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
2. Hyperglycemia.

Plan
Continue current insulin regimen. The patient will be instructed on monitoring blood glucose levels more frequently. We will re-evaluate the insulin dosage at the next appointment to address the hyperglycemia. The patient is advised to seek immediate medical attention if symptoms worsen.
explanations: Diabetes documented as poorly controlled, out of control, or with hyperglycemia is coded to diabetes with hyperglycemia.
Long-term insulin use in type 2 diabetes: add Z79.4.

distractors.why: Hyperglycemia is a complication with its own code.
Z79.4 is required for routine insulin use in type 2 diabetes.
